meanings.note: the present tense is normally left out: я мэр = I am the mayor
Present есть; у меня есть = I have. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to be; there is'.
future: буду / будешь ... + infinitive

examples.trans: You will be asking for forgiveness.

meanings.note: + prepositional (where). Core Russian prep meaning 'in, into' in everyday speech.
+ accusative (where to). Core Russian prep meaning 'in, into' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('important').

examples.text: Я тебе утром говорил: не торопись. Это очень важный вопрос.
examples.trans: I told you this morning: don't rush. It's a very important question.

meanings.note: Polite (вы) or plural. Core Russian det meaning 'your, yours (polite or plural)' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, who are your rivals?

meanings.note: The neuter form 'всё' used alone. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.
Neuter всё. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.
Plural все. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.
до вечера = until the evening; вечером = in the evening
E.g. a school evening. Common masculine noun meaning 'evening' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Добрый вечер, Вика. С Новым годом!
examples.trans: Good evening, Vika. Happy New Year!

meanings.note: instrumental of вечер used as an adverb

examples.trans: I'm at home in the evening.

meanings.note: Prefix 'во-' ('into, up') marks inward or upward movement (stem 'лноваться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to worry'.
Pointing at something. Core Russian part meaning 'here, there (pointing)' in everyday speech.
Emphasis. Core Russian part meaning 'here, there (pointing)' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: All right, here you go. There, look.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'everything', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Я знаю всё в моём отеле.
examples.trans: I know everything in my hotel.

meanings.note: polite to one person, or to several people

meanings.en: other forms: вас (gen/acc), вам (dat), вами (instr), вас (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (polite or plural)' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

вызывать.gloss: to cause, to raise; to call

meanings.en: to cause, to arouse, to raise
meanings.note: вызывать подозрения = to raise suspicion
вызывать полицию / врача = to call the police / a doctor

examples.text: Марина Сергеевна, упаковка маскирующая. Не вызывает подозрений.
examples.trans: Marina Sergeyevna, the packaging is camouflage. It doesn't raise suspicion.

meanings.note: + genitive. Core Russian prep meaning 'until, before; up to' in everyday speech.
Core Russian prep meaning 'until, before; up to' in everyday speech.

related.gloss: to reach, walk as far as

meanings.note: adds emphasis to the word before it

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

зайти.gloss: to come in, to drop in

meanings.en: to come in, to step in
meanings.note: Into a room. Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to come in, to drop in', paired with 'заходить'.
To visit briefly. Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to come in, to drop in', paired with 'заходить'.

examples.trans: I'll drop by in the evening.

examples.text: Ну, как хочешь. Лидия Алексеевна, зайдите, пожалуйста!
examples.trans: Well, as you like. Lidia Alekseyevna, come in, please!

meanings.note: Parenthetical. Core Russian adv meaning 'so, then, that means' in everyday speech.
verb: Что это значит? = What does it mean?
emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: вот именно = that's just it, quite right
А именно = namely. Core Russian part meaning 'exactly, namely, precisely' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Именно это я и хотел сказать.
examples.trans: That is justamente what I wanted to say.

examples.text: Вот именно. Но мне сдаваться нельзя.
examples.trans: Exactly. But I must not give up.

meanings.note: + dative. Core Russian prep meaning 'to, towards' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: There's someone here to see you.

examples.text: Аркадий Борисович, извините, тут к вам человек.
examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, I'm sorry, there's a man here to see you.

meanings.note: + infinitive. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'can, to be able', paired with 'смочь'.

examples.text: Этого не может быть. Это наша история.
examples.trans: That can't be. It's our history.

meanings.note: нас = us (gen/acc/prep); у нас = we have, at our place

meanings.en: other forms: нас (gen/acc), нам (dat), нами (instr), нас (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'we' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: + prepositional: на сайте. Core Russian prep meaning 'on, onto; for' in everyday speech.
+ accusative: на второй срок. Core Russian prep meaning 'on, onto; for' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: наш, наша, наше, наши; agrees with the noun

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates
In a mistaken or improper manner. Negative prefix 'не-' ('un-, non-, not') (stem 'правильно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Луи, ты меня совсем неправильно понял!

meanings.note: hesitation, at the start of a sentence
Ну, папа!. Core Russian part meaning 'well; come on' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: accusative/genitive его (него after prepositions), dative ему (нему)
For masculine and neuter things. Core Russian pron meaning 'he; it' in everyday speech.

meanings.en: other forms: его (gen/acc), ему (dat), им (instr), нём (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'he; it' in everyday speech.

Used as an exclamation of approval. Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'лично'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Отлично, Ваня! Вот это твой образ!
examples.trans: Perfect, Vanya! That right there is your look!

meanings.note: С первого раза = the first time. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('first').

examples.text: Ты не понимаешь с первого раза?
examples.trans: You don't understand the first time?

examples.text: Ты что, с первого раза не понимаешь?
examples.trans: What, you don't understand the first time?

meanings.note: Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'купить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'bribed'.

examples.text: Кажется, они просто подкупили нашего шефа.
examples.trans: It seems they simply bribed our Chef.

examples.text: Шеф, на кухне поговаривают, что вас подкупили.
examples.trans: Chef, people in the kitchen are saying you were bribed.

meanings.en: to disgrace oneself, make a fool of oneself
meanings.note: Intransitive reflexive verb. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'зориться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to disgrace oneself', paired with 'опозориться'.

examples.trans: Stop humiliating yourself in front of everyone!

examples.text: Он не хотел позориться на сцене.
examples.trans: He did not want to disgrace himself on stage.

examples.text: Встань прямо и не позорься тут.
examples.trans: Stand up straight and do not disgrace yourself here.

meanings.note: Takes на/в + accusative. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'лезть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to climb, start climbing', paired with 'лезть'.

examples.trans: Why did you climb onto the roof?

examples.text: Что вы, Клавдия Викторовна! Ладно, я сам полезу.
examples.trans: Oh stop it, Klavdia Viktorovna! Fine, I'll climb up myself.

meanings.note: Понял? = got it?; понял = got it. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'нять'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to understand', paired with 'понимать'.

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.note: Core Russian adv meaning 'then, later, afterwards' in everyday speech.
Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'сто-напросто'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Значит, штаны просто-напросто сами могли упасть!
examples.trans: That means the pants could have simply fallen down by themselves!

examples.text: Костя сказал это совершенно просто-напросто и спокойно.
examples.trans: Kostya said this quite simply and calmly.

meanings.note: Inanimate masculine noun. Common masculine noun meaning 'belt, strap' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: A leather strap on the watch.

examples.text: Пожалуйста, не затягивайте ремень слишком сильно.
examples.trans: Please do not tighten the strap too tightly.

meanings.note: Сам, сама, само, сами. Core Russian pron meaning 'oneself (myself, yourself...)' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Я и сама хорошо проведу время.
examples.trans: I'll have a good time on my own.

meanings.note: Literally 'until the meeting'. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'видание'). Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'meeting; date' in everyday Russian.

Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'видание'). Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'meeting; date' in everyday Russian.

Someone who saw what happened. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'видетель'). Agent/instrument noun formed with the productive Slavic suffix '-тель' ('-er'). Common masculine noun meaning 'witness' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: So that there are witnesses, Samson.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ходиться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to match, add up'.

examples.text: На кухне никто не хочет сходиться без причины.
examples.trans: In the kitchen nobody wants to match without a reason.

meanings.note: At the start of a question. Core Russian part meaning 'so, then; like that' in everyday speech.
Core Russian part meaning 'so, then; like that' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: So I shouldn't wait for you?
So I shouldn't wait for you tonight?

meanings.note: To someone you call ты. Core Russian det meaning 'your (informal)' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Я бы на твоём месте подумал.
examples.trans: If I were you, I'd think about it.

meanings.note: As opposed to before. Core Russian adv meaning 'now (from now on)' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Теперь я начальник нашей стройки. Ты уволен!
examples.trans: Now I'm the boss of our building site. You're fired!

meanings.note: At that time. Core Russian adv meaning 'then, back then' in everyday speech.
Core Russian adv meaning 'then, back then' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Я тебе тогда сказал: ты меня ещё поцелуешь.
examples.trans: I told you back then: you'll kiss me one day.

meanings.note: Core Russian adv meaning 'too, also' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Мы же здесь выросли. И о людях тоже надо думать.
examples.trans: After all, we grew up here. And you have to think about people too.

meanings.note: The one over there. Core Russian det meaning 'that' in everyday speech.
in 'то, что ...' = 'what, the thing that'
+ genitive. Core Russian prep meaning 'at, by; (у меня) I have' in everyday speech.
Possession. Core Russian prep meaning 'at, by; (у меня) I have' in everyday speech.
Просить у кого. Core Russian prep meaning 'at, by; (у меня) I have' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: уже четыре года = for four years now

examples.text: Я уже четыре года работаю мэром.
examples.trans: I've been mayor for four years now.

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'лика'). Common feminine noun meaning 'evidence / clues' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: We just fell asleep and just woke up.
Let's go destroy the evidence quickly.

meanings.note: Perfective of падать. Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'пасть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to fall, to drop', paired with 'падать'.

examples.trans: The cup fell off the table.

examples.text: А потом на меня упал мусор с ветки.
examples.trans: And then rubbish fell on me from a branch.

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to kiss'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense. The reflexive suffix '-ся'/'-сь' makes the action intransitive, reciprocal, or directed at the subject.

examples.trans: They were kissing for a long time.

examples.text: Ты вчера целовался с моей девушкой!

examples.trans: You were kissing right in the restaurant!

meanings.note: 3rd-declension feminine noun in -ь. Common feminine noun meaning 'honour; (Ваша честь) Your Honour' in everyday Russian.
Ваша честь = courtroom address to a judge

examples.text: Ваша честь, у нас есть заявление.
examples.trans: Your Honour, we have a statement.
It is a matter of honour.

examples.text: Ваша честь, у нас есть важное заявление.
examples.trans: Your Honour, we have an important statement.

meanings.note: Pluralia tantum. Common masculine noun meaning 'pants, trousers' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Are the pants too long for Slavik?

examples.text: Ты почему стоишь передо мной без штанов?
examples.trans: Why are you standing in front of me without pants?

meanings.note: pointing at a thing or a situation; 'это' + noun = 'this is ...'
points at something: это моё = that's mine
Linking word: главное — это народ. Core Russian pron meaning 'this, that; it is' in everyday speech.

meanings.en: other forms: этого, этому, это, этим, этом
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'this, that; it is' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.note: alone: 'я этого не хочу' = I don't want that

examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat.

examples.text: Меня уже тошнит от этой коммуналки! У нас труба уже неделю течёт.
examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat! Our pipe has been leaking for a week now.

meanings.note: меня = me (genitive/accusative), мне = to me (dative)

meanings.en: other forms: меня (gen/acc), мне (dat), мной (instr), мне (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'I' in everyday speech.
